title: C12 user profile v0 (per-user POLICY)
description: Response body of storage's per-user profile read `GET /users/{user_id}/profile`, minted by D18 (2026-07-26) as the contract home for D17's home_tz. This row holds POLICY — values the SYSTEM reads to decide its own behaviour for this user (scheduling, fallbacks) — and never user-facing identity or presentation, which belong to the input service. It is deliberately distinct from the per-record device_tz FACT carried on C2 source{}: the fact says where the user physically was at a moment and is correct under travel; the policy says when this user's night is. Absent profile => 404. There is no server-side default timezone anywhere in the system (D17), so a user with no home_tz is NOT schedulable — an operational alert, never a silent skip.

user_id.description: The user this profile belongs to. Per-user isolation is enforced by storage on the read.

home_tz.description: IANA zone id (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'), REQUIRED. Two jobs and no others: (a) SCHEDULING — deciding when this user's nightly consolidation fires, a question asked before any of that night's records exist; (b) FALLBACK — the zone a day-log block is rendered in when no contributing record carried a device_tz. It is NOT part of C10's range arithmetic, which is a plain UTC duration query needing no zone at all. ABBREVIATIONS ARE REJECTED: 'PST'/'MST' are ambiguous and DST-sensitive (D17); the pattern requires a region/city form, which structurally excludes them. THE PATTERN IS A CHEAP SHAPE GATE, NOT THE AUTHORITY: only tzdata resolution (zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(value)) can say whether an id exists, and storage MUST perform it on write, exactly as recording already does at the capture edge (unknown IANA id => 400). Bare 'UTC' is admitted because it is a real, unambiguous, DST-free zone id — but it is also the shape a lazy default takes, and D17 abolished default timezones, so a profile that says UTC should be one somebody chose. STORAGE NEVER WRITES THIS ON ITS OWN: home_tz is DECLARED, NOT INFERRED (corrected 2026-07-27; D18's first draft had storage auto-seed it from the first device-reported device_tz). The user sets it; a client may SUGGEST the device's current zone in a UI, but a guess is never stored as though it were an answer. It therefore does NOT move when the user travels: a week in Tokyo changes every record's device_tz and changes nothing here, so the consolidation boundary stays put instead of jumping 9h and producing a 15h night followed by a 33h one. That is the FACT/POLICY split working as designed.

profile_version.description: Monotone counter, bumped on every write. Lets a reader detect that policy changed under it (e.g. a scheduler that cached a fire time).

updated_at.description: RFC3339 UTC instant of the last write. UTC-canonical like every other timestamp in the system.
